### Summary

Reusable exec approvals could authorize changed arguments. In affected versions on macOS and Linux, selecting Allow Always for one exact command persisted a path-only grant. Later uses of the same executable with different arguments could therefore run without a new prompt.

This advisory is scoped to generated Allow Always entries. It does not treat operator-authored path-only allowlist rules as exact-argument grants; the failed boundary was OpenClaw broadening an exact command approved by the operator when it persisted that grant.

### Impact

After an operator approved a benign command, later untrusted content that influenced the agent could reuse its executable with different target or output arguments. Depending on the tool, this could send local files, overwrite user-writable files, or reach internal services without showing another approval prompt. Exploitation requires a prior persistent approval for the same executable.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, use one-time approval for commands whose arguments select network targets, input files, or output paths, and remove generated broad Allow Always entries.
summary: Reusable exec approvals could authorize changed arguments
